title: Decoding Baby Cries and Safe Sleep Engineering
summary: Crying is the baby's only language for expressing their needs: hunger, colic and gas, a wet nappy, or overstimulation and heat. To soothe the baby, use the well-known five-step technique: safe swaddling, holding the baby on their side or stomach in your arms (for soothing only, never for sleep), white noise (mimicking the sound of the womb), steady rocking, and sucking. For safe sleep: the baby must always sleep on their back in a separate cot beside the parents, with no pillows or soft toys, for strict protection against sudden infant death syndrome.
try_this: This week: practise correct swaddling together (securing the arms while leaving the baby's hips and legs completely free, to avoid hip dislocation), and prepare a source of gentle white noise or soft, steady Qur'an recitation in the bedroom.
reflection_prompts: What will you do if the baby keeps crying after you have checked they are clean and fed?
Does your baby's cot meet safe sleep standards (free of heavy blankets and pillows)?
